script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. ASCENSION CORPORATE OFFICE - DAY

We open on a bustling corporate office, filled with employees rushing about, typing on computers, and making phone calls. In the center of it all is our PROTAGONIST, JAMES, in his late 30s, wearing a suit and tie. He looks tired and uninspired as he sits at his cubicle.

JAMES (to himself): Another day in the rat race...

Suddenly, his boss, MR. WILLIAMS, appears at his cubicle.

MR. WILLIAMS: (exasperated) James, I need you in my office. Now.

INT. MR. WILLIAMS' OFFICE - DAY

James enters Mr. Williams' office, where the boss is seated behind his desk, looking stern.

MR. WILLIAMS: (frustrated) You're not living up to your potential, James. I can't afford to have dead weight on my team. You have two weeks to find a new job or I'll have to let you go.

EXT. CITY STREET - DAY

James walks out of the office building, feeling lost and defeated. He stops at a crosswalk, looking around at the hustle and bustle of the city.

JAMES: (to himself) This isn't what I wanted. I need a change.

Suddenly, he notices a flyer in a tree for a local culinary school. An idea sparks in his mind.

INT. KITCHEN CLASSROOM - NIGHT

James is now enrolled in the culinary school, surrounded by other students. His instructor, CHEF MARTINEZ, is a stern but fair mentor.

CHEF MARTINEZ: (to the class) Cooking is an art, not just a job. You have to put your heart and soul into every dish.

James listens intently, determined to learn and grow.

INT. ASCENSION CORPORATE OFFICE - ONE MONTH LATER

James returns to the Ascension corporate office, but this time as a successful chef at a new restaurant. He walks in with confidence and pride, wearing a chef's jacket instead of a suit and tie.

MR. WILLIAMS: (surprised) James? What are you doing here?

JAMES: (smiling) I found my passion, Mr. Williams. I'm a chef now.

MR. WILLIAMS: (impressed) I had no idea you had it in you. I'm glad you found what you love.

INT. RESTAURANT KITCHEN - NIGHT

James stands in the kitchen, surrounded by his team, preparing for another busy night. He looks content and fulfilled.

JAMES: (to himself) This is where I belong.

FADE OUT.

THE END
